title: Innovation in Blueberry Growing: The Impact of Organic Fertilization
metaDescription: Discover how scientific research explores new organic fertilization techniques and regulators to improve blueberry yield.
excerpt: A recent scientific study analyzes how combining organic fertilization with growth regulators improves yield and water efficiency in blueberry crops.
imageAlt: Fresh blueberry plant in a high-mountain agricultural setting

blocks.text: Modern agricultural production faces important challenges because of water scarcity and the risk of soil degradation caused by excessive use of chemical fertilizers. In this scenario, achieving blueberry production that is green, sustainable and highly water-efficient has become a priority for researchers and farmers worldwide. Understanding how to optimize natural resources and improve growing practices is essential to ensure the future of this delicious fruit without compromising ecosystems.
What the source says: key findings on fertilization and regulators

A recent study published on the scientific platform evaluated the effects of combining different types of fertilizers — chemical, organic and biofertilizers — with different concentrations of a plant growth regulator called brassinolide-type brazide, covering the study periods of 2022 and 2023. The researchers observed that the specific treatment combining organic manure with 3 µmol l -1 of brazide significantly lowered the lodging index and lodging rate of the plant stems by 25.8% and 31.5% respectively, thanks to changes in their morphological structure and to greater soil respiration.

Likewise, this treatment optimized water-use efficiency and substantially reduced crop evapotranspiration and greenhouse gas emissions. The authors also recorded notable improvements in leaf area index, root growth, nitrogen uptake and overall plant yield, increasing the number of new shoots and flower buds compared with the unfertilized control group.
Context: how this research fits with traditional fruit management

These findings are in line with the agricultural industry’s constant search to reduce environmental impact through practices that respect the land’s natural cycles. Historically, growing berries such as blueberries has depended on a constant supply of water and nutrients; however, semi-arid stress conditions and water scarcity call for smarter alternatives. The balanced use of organic manures together with compounds that strengthen the plant’s mechanical resistance shows that it is possible to boost crop development under adverse weather conditions without saturating the soil with unnecessary chemicals.
What it means for you: understanding the origin of what we eat

For blueberry lovers, knowing about this scientific research helps appreciate the enormous agronomic effort behind each fruit. Although this type of study focuses mainly on production scale and technical optimization for farmers, it reminds us of the importance of prioritizing food grown with rigorous, environmentally respectful methods. Knowing that science backs more efficient farming practices reinforces our peace of mind when choosing products grown with care and environmental awareness.

Agricultural science keeps showing that innovation and respect for nature can go hand in hand to obtain exceptional harvests.
